comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the rejection of the nuclear-escape hypothesis showing adenoviruses clustering with Mavericks rather than NCLDVs. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical strength (posterior probability 0.94, strong hypothesis test rejections C58-C65), while peer reviewers describe 'convincing' and 'compelling' phylogenetic analyses. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C121 which OpenEval places in R6.

Perfect agreement on virophage monophyly (C8, C45-C46, C53-C54, C77). Both evaluations note strong statistical support (posterior probability = 1, bootstrap = 95%) and accept this validates family Lavidaviridae. OpenEval provides more technical detail about concatenated vs single-protein analyses, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting expanded sequence sampling. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the basal placement of virophages (C9, C48-C51, C78). OpenEval notes moderate statistical support (54% Bayesian, 73% ML bootstrap) and acknowledges uncertainty with alternative placements. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the 'virophage-first' hypothesis as best supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED despite OpenEval noting some uncertainty. Peer review includes C92 which OpenEval places in R7.

Complete agreement on independent acquisition of rve-integrase (C7, C111-C118, C122). Both evaluations accept the parsimony analysis and character distribution evidence. OpenEval provides detailed reasoning about phylogenetic distribution patterns, while peer reviewers accept without specific objection as part of 'convincing phylogenetic analyses.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the phylogenetic evidence contradicting nuclear-escape predictions regarding cytoplasmic linear plasmid proteins (C66-C71, C74-C76). OpenEval details how these proteins cluster with eukaryotic sequences rather than NCLDV proteins, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'compelling analyses' against nuclear-escape. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the overall evolutionary model conclusions (C10, C120, C123). OpenEval notes these logically follow from empirical findings, while peer reviewers describe this as 'an important step' in understanding viral evolution. Peer review includes C124-C125 (speculative model elements) which OpenEval places in R12. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on the quantitative MCMC results examining alternative root placements (C84-C87). Both evaluations accept the 27.4% alternative root support and 0% nuclear-escape support. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate scientific uncertainty, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through acknowledgment of 'virophage-first' as best supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the ancient timing inference (C88-C91). OpenEval details the logic connecting NCLDV age estimates to virophage divergence, while peer reviewers accept the 'ancient evolutionary history' framing. OpenEval includes C93 which peer review places in R13. Peer review includes C11 (arms-race characterization) which OpenEval evaluates separately as UNCERTAIN in R17. Both rate as SUPPORTED for timing claims.

Both address the speculative evolutionary model (C94-C99, C102-C104, C108-C110). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting substantial speculation about ancestral states not directly tested, though clearly labeled as 'Ideas and speculation.' Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating these as reasonable interpretations without challenge. This represents a difference in evaluation stringency: OpenEval distinguishes speculation from tested hypotheses, while peer reviewers accept speculation within appropriate framing.

Perfect agreement on dataset composition and sampling methodology (C126-C128). Both evaluations accept the expanded dataset and subsampling approach. OpenEval describes as 'straightforward methodological descriptions,' while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'larger number of sequences to better represent diversity.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the background characterization of bamfordviruses (C1-C2, C12-C26). OpenEval notes these are well-established, literature-based claims with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the foundational characterization. Peer review includes C27 which OpenEval places in R6. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on the accurate description of competing hypotheses from literature (C3-C5, C28-C41). Both evaluations accept these as well-cited descriptions that set up the study's hypothesis testing. OpenEval notes correct identification of predictions and limitations, while peer reviewers accept as accurate representations. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the technical phylogenetic findings about single-protein analyses and phylogenetic conflict (C56-C57). OpenEval notes appropriate handling of conflicting signal, while peer reviewers accept as supporting details. Peer review includes C47 (PLV polyphyly) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R10. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the observation of PLV polyphyly (C47). OpenEval describes as clear observation from tree topologies, while peer reviewers accept without challenge as part of 'convincing phylogenetic analyses.' Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the use of prior literature to contextualize findings (C73, C105-C107, C119). OpenEval notes appropriate citation and use for supporting arguments, while peer reviewers accept these connecting interpretations as part of understanding 'constraints and main drivers of virus evolution.' Peer review includes additional claims (C79-C83, C93) about inferences from phylogenetic results. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both support the logical inferences from virophage basal placement (C80-C82, C92). OpenEval notes these are reasonable inferences from phylogenetic evidence though speculative about ancestral lifestyles. Peer reviewers accept without objection as part of broader interpretive framework. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations of the 'arms-race' characterization (C11). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this interpretive framework implies coevolutionary dynamics not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the ancient timescale and evolutionary interaction framing without distinguishing the 'arms-race' terminology as requiring separate validation. This reflects different standards for interpretive language.
